headline: SpaceXAI launches Grok Bot, AI agents that do real work for $120/month
summary: Grok Bot acts as a persistent AI teammate, signing into your tools to complete tasks autonomously. It's now in beta for select subscribers.
details: SpaceXAI has released an early beta of Grok Bot, an AI agent designed to move beyond simple prompts and continuously execute tasks across user applications. The core concept is to create persistent Bots with specific job functions, grant them access to software and websites, and delegate work like a human colleague.

Each Bot operates within its own computing environment, can continue working even when a user's laptop is closed, and can return for approval or to report completion. SpaceXAI states the system was initially an internal prototype that proved effective across various company teams for tasks like sales, marketing, and bug fixing.

Grok Bot aims to differentiate itself with a management model for agents, featuring persistent workers with responsibilities, memory, learned routines, and the ability to collaborate with other Bots. This allows for complex, multi-step workflows to be handled by AI.

The beta version is available today, August 11, for SuperGrok Heavy, Cursor Ultra, and Cursor Premium Teams subscribers. It supports macOS, Windows, Linux, and iOS, with an Android version planned for the future.

Pricing for Grok Bot varies: Cursor Ultra is $200 per month for individuals, including a dedicated computer for the Bot and access to user tools. For organizations, Cursor Premium Teams costs $120 per seat per month, adding features like centralized billing and team analytics.

Existing SuperGrok Heavy subscribers ($300 per month) also get access. However, new organizations looking to sign up are directed to a waitlist. The pricing positions Grok Bot as a significant investment, raising questions about its ability to replace manual labor or traditional automation to justify the per-user cost.

headline: WhatsApp link generation server shipped with no API key required
summary: A new open MCP server allows AI agents to generate WhatsApp links and QR codes without needing an API key or signup.
details: Developers can now easily generate WhatsApp links and QR codes for AI agents without the hassle of API keys or signups. A new open MCP server, available via whatsusernames.link, provides this functionality directly.

Previously, generating these links often involved scraping Stack Overflow for regex or writing custom validation functions. This new server integrates seamlessly, allowing AI agents to call it as a native tool.

The server offers a free, public REST API and an MCP endpoint, both with IP-rate limiting (60 requests/min for JSON tools, 20 for QR generation). This ensures fair usage while providing immediate access.
By offering a zero-friction MCP endpoint for WhatsApp tooling, the developers aim to become the go-to solution for AI agents, preventing them from reinventing this common functionality.
This move aligns with the vision that many AI agent interactions will eventually route through MCP servers, similar to how APIs handle search traffic today.
